macro_summary: Markets are navigating a convergence of rate pressure, semiconductor sentiment deterioration, and a geopolitical oil supply shock heading into tomorrow's FOMC decision. The Nasdaq fell 0.8% Monday and SOX dropped 5.9% as AI-slowdown commentary from Altman, Amodei, and Musk weighed on chip names, while energy is the lone sector with meaningful positive momentum on WTI above $103/bbl. The binary Fed event tomorrow—with the dot plot potentially signaling two additional hikes—is the dominant near-term risk factor across all five consensus ideas. Kalshi implies 86.5 percent hike / 11.5 percent hold on Sep 16; September CPI above 0.3 percent priced at 95.5 percent.
screening_note: 6 independent overnight screening runs analyzed; minimum threshold to qualify was 2 appearances. All 5 ideas cleared that bar, with SKHY reaching maximum consensus at 6/6 runs.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. (ADR)
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 6 of 6 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction — the strongest consensus signal in this digest. The stock sold off with the broad chip sector Monday (-3%+) despite company-specific positives that are unrelated to AI-slowdown fears: a 40 trillion won buyback, a Temasek sovereign capital injection, and an emerging global DRAM shortage that underpins pricing power. At ~$190, SKHY trades at a ~30% discount to the analyst consensus target of $247.67, with Bernstein and Citi both reaffirming Buy in September 2026 and ROIC above 70% on an improving memory cycle.
ideas.catalyst: Micron (MU) earnings Sep 30 as near-term memory sector read-through; SKHY Q3 DRAM shipment guidance expected imminently; FOMC hold on Sep 16 removes a rate headwind
ideas.edge: Analyst consensus target $247.67 vs last close ~$190 = ~30% implied upside gap; 40T won buyback + Temasek injection are hard, quantifiable shareholder return catalysts; ROIC >70%
ideas.bull_case: DRAM shortage tightens supply, buyback provides price floor, and a Fed hold tomorrow catalyzes a semi sector re-rating — SKHY re-rates toward the $247 consensus target over the Oct/Nov earnings window.
ideas.bear_case: A hawkish Fed hike with aggressive dot plot accelerates broad semiconductor rotation out; AI slowdown narrative bleeds into memory demand fears even if fundamentally unsupported.

ideas.name: Microsoft Corporation
ideas.thesis: MSFT appeared in 5 of 6 overnight screens and showed unusual relative strength on Monday — gaining 2% while the Nasdaq fell 0.8% — signaling institutional accumulation into the FOMC binary. The stock is coiled just below the $500 psychological level with Azure growing at 43% and a $678B commercial backlog (up 84% YoY), providing durable earnings power into a late October earnings catalyst. A Fed hold or non-aggressive dot plot tomorrow could serve as the unlock for a breakout above $500 toward the $588.97 analyst consensus target.
ideas.catalyst: FOMC resolution Sep 16 (rate clarity re-rates long-duration growth); next earnings ~late Oct 2026; Azure $100B annual run-rate milestone
ideas.edge: Consensus 12-month price target $588.97 vs ~$498 close = ~18% gap; Wedbush target $625; Azure 43% growth + $678B commercial backlog up 84%; beat Q2 with $81.3B revenue +17% YoY
ideas.bull_case: Post-FOMC clarity removes the rate overhang, $500 breakout triggers institutional momentum buying, and Azure's AI cloud compounding sustains a 13%+ EPS growth trajectory into October earnings.
ideas.bear_case: A hawkish dot plot signals two more hikes, compressing long-duration tech multiples regardless of Azure fundamentals; $498 support breaks and stock retests lower levels ahead of earnings.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust
ideas.thesis: QQQ appeared in 5 of 6 screens as a tactical hedge, not a directional long — specifically via short-dated put or put-spread structures. The Nasdaq 100 is disproportionately exposed to the FOMC binary given semiconductors comprise ~42% of the tech sector and are already under dual pressure from AI-slowdown sentiment and a near-certain rate hike. Kalshi prices the hike at 86.5% meaning the real tail risk is a hawkish dot plot signaling two additional hikes, which could gap QQQ materially lower and is not yet fully priced.
ideas.catalyst: FOMC decision Sep 16, 2:00 PM ET — dot plot release; markets pricing possible hike to 3.75-4.00%; 10-yr yield briefly above 5%
ideas.edge: Nasdaq 100 already down 0.8% Monday; SOX -5.9%; AI safety narrative + potential hawkish dot plot = binary event within 24 hours; near-term put options relatively cheap vs realized vol spike potential
ideas.bull_case: A hold or dovish-leaning hold surprises markets; QQQ puts expire worthless but provide clean portfolio protection at low cost into the resolution.
ideas.bear_case: Hawkish dot plot signals aggressive tightening path; QQQ gaps down sharply on tech multiple compression; put spread pays out meaningfully as semis lead the decline.

ideas.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
ideas.thesis: XLE appeared in 4 of 6 overnight screens as the cleanest macro hedge in a difficult tape — energy is the only major S&P sector with strong positive momentum (XLE +28-48% YTD) while the rest of the market sells off. The Saudi East-West pipeline closure, collapsed Iran-Gulf diplomatic talks, and WTI above $103/bbl create a structural supply deficit that the IEA estimates at 12.8M bbl/day, keeping crude elevated regardless of the Fed outcome. Energy also acts as a natural inflation hedge if the Fed hikes hawkishly.
ideas.catalyst: FOMC decision Sep 16 (energy as inflation hedge into hike); Saudi East-West pipeline closure ongoing with no near-term resolution; Brent ~$105, WTI ~$103-104
ideas.edge: XLE +28-48% YTD vs SPY flat-to-negative; energy earnings consensus +57% in 2026; 3.12% dividend yield adds return cushion; oil up ~4.7% in a single session Monday
ideas.bull_case: Pipeline closure persists, Iran talks remain stalled, and crude holds above $100 — XLE delivers sector-leading earnings growth and dividend yield while acting as a portfolio hedge against a hawkish Fed.
ideas.bear_case: Surprise Iran deal or unexpected OPEC supply release breaks crude below $95; a severe Fed-induced demand destruction narrative pressures oil alongside equities.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in 2 of 6 overnight screens — the minimum threshold — qualifying as a watchlist idea rather than a high-conviction consensus trade. The stock dropped ~3.4% Monday on AI-slowdown commentary from Altman, Amodei, and Musk, a sentiment-driven move disconnected from fundamentals: hyperscaler capex commitments remain above $600B in 2026 and NVDA trades at ~21x forward earnings, in-line with the S&P 500 despite its dominant AI chip position. Both runs recommended a defined-risk call spread rather than outright stock, and both explicitly flagged waiting for post-FOMC clarity before sizing.
ideas.catalyst: Micron (MU) earnings Sep 30 as semi sector read-through; Q1 FY2027 NVDA earnings estimated late Nov 2026; post-FOMC clarity Sep 16-17
ideas.edge: Stock down ~5% in 2 sessions on sentiment not fundamentals; 21x forward P/E at S&P parity despite dominant market position; premarket stabilization +0.6% suggesting dip absorption
ideas.bull_case: AI-slowdown narrative fades post-FOMC, hyperscaler capex confirms intact, and NVDA mean-reverts toward recent highs — a call spread captures the bounce with defined downside.
ideas.bear_case: Fed hike + hawkish dot plot compounds AI sentiment pressure; SOX continues its -19% drawdown from ATH; NVDA's premium collapses further if AI capex guidance weakens at any hyperscaler.
